analysis.title: $3 Trillion In Two Days: Goldman's Molavi Says Crowded Funds Played "Stop Bingo" Until Everything Broke
key_insights: Week ending Nov 6, 2026: S&P 500 -2.68% to 7,377, Nasdaq -3.37%, Russell 2000 -2.05%, Dow -0.94%. The path was far more violent than the weekly change implies: relief rally Wednesday after the Democratic sweep, air pocket Thursday, partial rebound Friday.

Molavi attributes the drop mainly to a negative feedback loop between performance and technicals. P&L losses triggered technical stops, which forced short-duration, tightly managed, often leveraged strategies to degross or liquidate ('stop bingo').

Thursday Nov 5: S&P -4.4%, Dow -1,833 points, Nasdaq -6.3% (worst session since the pandemic reaction), VIX up roughly 70%, all eleven sectors lower. Nvidia lost more than $440B of market value. The selloff was partly pinned on fears of tighter AI and data-center regulation under the new Congress.
VIX had the largest two-day round trip on record: -3.59 points then +4.96, total 8.55 points on Nov 5, versus the prior record of 7.87 in April 2013.
Goldman's Tadayon: Wednesday and Thursday were a '$3tr event'. US equity market cap fell from $75 trillion to under $72 trillion. US market cap is still up about $5 trillion, or ~7%, YTD.

Gross exposure had fallen going into November but concentration had not, so degrossing hit the same names that had triggered the stops. Long/short funds had a very hard 4-6 weeks, and the losses spread to multi-asset, systematic, credit and convertible strategies.

Goldman prime book: net selling in global Info Tech for Oct 30-Nov 5 was about -3% of sector gross market value, matching the most extreme weekly selling in the decade-long series. Tech hedge funds erased their entire 2026 gain by Thursday night. Privorotsky called it the biggest gross cut in US long/short TMT since Covid and the biggest net cut since Liberation Day.

Spread and pair trades broke down: software vs semis, AAPL vs Nasdaq, banks vs insurance, European banks vs European defense, defensives vs growth, small vs large, Europe vs US, S&P ex-AI vs S&P. Spreads blew out and correlations broke.

Crowding was high before the break. Goldman PB risk data showed realized 3m alpha correlations between fundamental and systematic L/S managers in the top decile of the past decade, and US/Asia fundamental manager correlations at all-time highs, largely driven by the AI trade.

AI vs SPX or Nasdaq did not work as a hedge, and the short book was squeezed as money rotated into defensives. Momentum gave back all of its 2026 gains while value rallied. Morgan Stanley prime brokerage counted a record 70% tech momentum crash.

Volume was not liquidity. QQQ set a notional volume record of $86B on Thursday, and US-listed ETF notional volume was about $580B, second only to the 2024 spike. Nearly $7 trillion notional of S&P and Nasdaq futures traded last week, a record. Nomura's McElligott counted a $165B mechanical purge.

Rotation went into value, small and mid caps, under-owned defensives and stable cash flows (staples, real estate, healthcare, consumer, travel). Weeks ago the S&P was up 12-13% while most members were down on the year.

Semis are down ~28% over the last month, one of the largest rolling one-month drawdowns on record, comparable to 2001, 2008 and March 2020 (Callahan). The SOX fell more than 12% last week. Largest losers: Lumentum (LITE) -36%, Seagate (STX) -28%, Marvell (MRVL) -28%, Western Digital (WDC) -28%, SanDisk (SNDK) -27%.
The Nasdaq 100 bounced off a trendline that held in both the April 2025 and late-2025 selloffs. Molavi calls it 'key support level touched and reinforced…so far'.

Valuation: S&P staples' premium to the SPX is at its highest in 10+ years. The staples index trades at about 2x the 24-month forward multiple of semis. The staples-vs-SPX P/E spread hit 6.2 points on Thursday, versus peaks near 4.5 in 2016 and 2022.

The S&P is 'cheaper rather than cheap'. If last week was the trough, the S&P bottomed at 18x forward earnings, versus 10.4x in March 2009, 13.3x in March 2020 and 15.7x in October 2022 (ignores growth). Earnings are fine, but 'solid (and in some cases blowout) isn't enough'.

Nvidia: on Sunday Nov 8, CEO Jensen Huang admitted in a staff memo to an affair with a woman US officials have identified as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. The board opened an independent investigation and says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Beijing calls the allegations groundless. NVDA fell as much as 8% Monday before trimming losses while the rest of the Mag 7 and chips rallied.
Prediction markets put the odds of Huang leaving this year at 13%, after briefly touching about one third overnight. Three House GOP chairs want a closed-door briefing with Huang on Nov 18.

Street views are split on whether the selloff is over. JPMorgan's Lakos-Bujas sees it as nearly exhausted (momentum crowding fell from the 100th to the 76th percentile). Morgan Stanley's Wilson sees the correction nearing an end. Citi downgraded US equities and global tech in favor of Europe. Goldman models show $25B or more of potential CTA supply this week, with CPI and CoreWeave earnings due Tuesday Nov 10.

Molavi says next week will show whether Friday's stabilization was momentary or a new floor. The author leans 'momentary' because concentration remains, CTAs are not done selling, and Nvidia carries a CEO governance risk. The author also notes the next stop-bingo episode could occur on the short side given the staples valuation.

tension_points.bull_case: JPMorgan's Lakos-Bujas sees the selloff as nearly exhausted, with momentum crowding reset from the 100th to the 76th percentile. Morgan Stanley's Wilson sees the correction nearing an end. The Nasdaq 100 held a multi-year trendline, and earnings are solid.
tension_points.bear_case: Concentration remains the problem. Momentum crowding at the 76th percentile is reset only versus the summer extreme, Goldman models show $25B or more of CTA supply this week, and Nvidia carries a CEO governance risk. Citi downgraded US equities and global tech.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the Nasdaq 100 trendline that held in the April 2025 and late-2025 selloffs would undercut the 'new floor' read. Molavi says the coming week will show whether Friday was momentary or a new floor.

tension_points.bull_case: Money rotating into staples, healthcare, real estate and other under-owned defensives has offset the AI drawdown, and the index is 'cheaper rather than cheap' at 18x forward earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Staples' premium to the SPX is the highest in 10+ years and the sector trades at about 2x the semis' forward multiple, so the next stop-bingo episode could play out on the short side.

theme_stances.key_argument: A feedback loop between P&L losses and technical stops forced leveraged, short-duration strategies to degross, and the selling hit the same crowded names.
Semis fell about 28% in a month, and AI did not serve as a hedge against SPX or Nasdaq.
